questions.q: What does Microsoft Entra ID govern that Azure RBAC does not?
options: Only billing and cost management for the subscription
Access to a specific storage account or virtual machine
Nothing -- Entra ID and Azure RBAC govern exactly the same scope
Directory-level, tenant-wide identity and roles -- such as who can manage users or app registrations
questions.explain: Entra ID is the directory-level identity layer, governing the tenant itself (users, groups, app registrations, administrative roles like Purview Administrator), while Azure RBAC governs authorization at the resource level, covered in the next lesson.

questions.q: Where do you find built-in directory roles in the Microsoft Entra admin center?
options: Billing → Cost Management → Roles
Identity → Roles & admins → Roles & admins
Home → Resource groups → Roles
Settings → Subscriptions → Access control (IAM)
questions.explain: Every built-in directory role lives on the Roles and administrators page, reached via Identity → Roles & admins → Roles & admins in the Entra admin center.

questions.q: In the Add assignments pane, when does a checked principal actually become assigned to the role?
options: The moment you check the box next to their name
Automatically, 24 hours after being checked
Only after the principal manually accepts the role assignment
Only after you choose Add -- checking a principal just adds it to the Selected panel first
questions.explain: Checked principals accumulate in the "Selected" panel on the right, but nothing is actually assigned until you choose Add to commit the change.

questions.q: Why might a directory role be assigned to an app registration instead of a human user?
options: Because app registrations always receive the Global Administrator role by default
Because assigning roles to apps is required before any human can be assigned a role
App registrations cannot hold directory roles under any circumstances
So automated tooling like a classification job or Purview scan trigger gets exactly the permissions it needs, instead of borrowing a shared human credential
questions.explain: Automated governance tooling and service-to-service integrations need their own scoped permissions. Assigning a directory role directly to the app registration (service principal) avoids borrowing a shared or overly broad human credential.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend assigning directory roles to role-assignable groups rather than individuals one at a time?
options: Groups are the only principal type the Add assignments pane supports
Group membership changes don't require touching the role assignment itself
Individual role assignments are technically impossible in Entra ID
Assigning roles to groups removes the need for any audit logging
questions.explain: When a role is assigned to a group, adding or removing a person from that group automatically grants or revokes the role — no repeated per-person assignment needed, which is the same group-based pattern Lesson 10 covers in more depth.
